name: A Toronto lot

place_source.title: Wikidata: Toronto (Q172), coordinate location and elevation above sea level

blurb: A suburban Toronto lot on the Ontario plain: maples and redcedar over a lawn and shrub border, with a ravine edge of hemlock and yew behind, visited by robins, cardinals, chickadees and woodpeckers by day, by squirrels, chipmunks and raccoons after dark, and by painted turtles and northern water snakes where the garden pond meets the water table.

facts.text: Toronto has a hot summer humid continental climate (Köppen: Dfa), with warm, humid summers and cold winters.

source.title: Wikipedia: Toronto

facts.text: In the classification applied by Natural Resources Canada, the city of Toronto is in plant hardiness zone 7a, and some suburbs and nearby towns have lower zone ratings.

source.title: Wikipedia: Toronto
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Toronto", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Most ravine lands and river bank floodplains in Toronto are public parklands, which is where the city's mature tree cover survives.

source.title: Wikipedia: Toronto
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Toronto", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Since the 1950s raccoons have been present in metropolitan areas including Toronto, where the species uses urban areas as habitat.

source.title: Wikipedia: Raccoon

facts.text: The black, melanistic form of the eastern gray squirrel predominates in large parts of southeastern Canada, and black squirrels are frequently seen in Toronto's ravines and yards.

source.title: Wikipedia: Eastern gray squirrel
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Eastern gray squirrel", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: In March 2024, bald eagles were found nesting in Toronto for the first time.
